## APPENDICITIS WITHOUT PERFORATION
[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)
Patients with an acutely inflamed appendix and no gangrene or perforation are
considered to have uncomplicated appendicitis. Patients with gangrene,
perforation, peritonitis, or abscess have complicated appendicitis. Treatment
with antibiotics is an option for patients who are unfit for surgery or refuse
surgery. Treatment with antibiotics should not be used routinely as an
alternative to surgery.
## Select for treatment of complicated appendicitis
[Link to appendicitis with perforation menu](appendicitis-with-perforation)
## Treatment of uncomplicated appendicitis
Surgical management: Administer prophylaxis regimen below prior to surgery
only. Stop antibiotics after the surgery.
Surgical prophylaxis:
Cefazolin weight-based dosing preop < AND > metronidazole 500 mg IV once
Post-surgical: antibiotics not recommended after appendectomy
## Interval appendectomy or no appendectomy
Duration of therapy: Treat with antibiotics for 7 days total
Preferred:
## Inpatient [Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)
Healthcare-associated infection, critical illness, or immunosuppression:
[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)
Alternative:
[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)
Alternative for severe Beta-lactam reaction:
[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)
[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h) ## Outpatient Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDDS ##ER
